title: Bing Crosby at the Paramount and the film scale
summary: Thomas recalls Bing as extra attraction, Russ Columbo's rivalry, and film pay of ten dollars an hour thanks to Mills.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well, I think it could have happened... In retrospect, I think it could have happened maybe in this way. The first time that Bing Crosby played the Paramount Theatre, we were the stars, and Bing Crosby was the extra added attraction. So that might...
What year was that?
I don't know...
Was that Cab Calloway and His Orchestra or The Missourians?
Thomas (3) - 22
It was Cab Calloway. We'd got to Cab Calloway's Orchestra by then.
It was Cab Calloway's Orchestra, and Bing Crosby was the extra added...
Attraction yeah.
And where was this theatre?
At the Paramount.
And what year was that?

This was around '33 or '34. I don't know if it was before the picture or not, but it was around the same time we made the picture. Because see, Bing Crosby had met this guy Russ Columbo, and Russ Columbo had heard Bing sing. And Russ Columbo got to New York before Bing did. And he got popular. He didn't just get here before he did. He got popular. He got a little "buh-bu-buh-do" going, you know. And Bing Crosby didn't like him. He kind of hated Russ Columbo with a passion. But Bing Crosby made it. He came and started doing his thing and singing, so he made it on his own.
But I know the first theatre date he had in New York was with...he was on the bill with us -- but he was the extra added attraction. I don't know who played for him.
For Bing?
Thomas (3) - 23

Yeah. I don't know whether it was a pit band or what. But he went on before we did. Because we were the stars. We went on before he did. And Bing, he didn't have no stage presence at all. But he could sing. He'd just walk... He'd walk out on the stage and do it. Because see, Bing used to be with Paul Whiteman, who...
Oh, he had left Paul Whiteman then??
Yes, he left Paul Whiteman.
Well, that's got to be like 1934.
Yeah, around 1934. Because I think that's before we made the pictures. Then Bing got...
Because I think he left Paul Whiteman in 1933.
Yeah. Because Bing Crosby got big on account of he was on the radio... See, in those days it was only radio.
That's right.

And he got big on the radio. So they brought him in to do this show with us. And this was a big deal. Then when we did the movie with him, he got us... Because we were hot. We were kind of hot then. They don't show that picture much.
They did the movie, then. They don't show that movie.
No, we didn't...
Thomas (3) - 24
The next one...the one we did later with Woody Herman's band, the big band, with Eleanor Powell and W.C. Fields. They show that one quite a bit now.

Yeah, I haven't seen that one. See, we recorded that week. We recorded, and they took pictures... They did the movie while we were recording. And you know, the musicians' scale for that was ten dollars an hour. We made so much money... We had never made that kind of money. We had never made a picture before. We never made that kind of money before. And I always give Mills credit for that, because Mills was in a (?) where he could get in and get them big deals for us.
